questions.s:
Answer:better

Explanation:
The sentence is making a comparison between two points in time — when they left for Mexico and now.
When comparing two things, we use the comparative form of adjectives.

  • The word "good" becomes "better" in the comparative form.

  • Saying "in good condition than..." is incorrect — it should be "in better condition than..."

Let’s review the options:

  • better → ✅ Correct comparative form of "good"

  • excellent → ❌ Not a comparative; also not used with "than"

  • more good → ❌ Incorrect (never use "more" with "good"; use "better")

  • best → ❌ Superlative form, used when comparing more than two

Correct sentence:
When they left for Mexico, their house was in better condition than it is now.

questions.q: Which of the following CANNOT be put under the classification of adjectives?
questions.s:
On the basis of how adjectives describe a noun/pronoun, they are classified as:

• Adjectives of Quality - describes kind or quality of a person or thing.

• Adjectives of Quantity - shows how much of a thing is meant.

• Adjectives of Number - shows how many persons or things are meant, or in what order a person or thing stands.

• Demonstrative Adjectives - points out which person or thing is meant.

• Interrogative Adjectives - used with nouns to ask questions.

Hence, option (b) is correct.

questions.q:
Select the sentence with the most appropriate Superlative degree.

(SSC MTS 2024 S.33_22-Oct_Shift-1)
o: She is the talentedest musician in the orchestra.
She is the talent of all musicians in the orchestra.
She is the most talented musician in the orchestra.
She is more talented musician in the orchestra.
questions.s:
Answer: She is the most talented musician in the orchestra.

Explanation:
When comparing qualities in a group, the superlative degree is used to show the highest level of that quality.

  • "Most talented" is the correct superlative form of "talented."

  • "Talentedest" is incorrect because superlatives for adjectives with three or more syllables are formed with "most," not by adding "-est."

  • "She is the talent of all musicians" is incorrect and does not use comparative or superlative forms properly.

  • "She is more talented musician" is incorrect because "more talented" needs "a" or "the" before "musician" (e.g., "a more talented musician").

Therefore, the correct sentence is:
"She is the most talented musician in the orchestra."

It turned out to be the noisy park party anybody had ever attended.

questions.s: The adjective "noisy" should be placed before the noun "party". Also, the word "anybody" should be in the correct form as "anyone" for better clarity and flow. The sentence structure needs to be modified to use the proper comparative form: "the most noisy" or "the noisiest".

questions.q: The given sentence is divided into three segments. Select the option that has the segment with a grammatical error. If there is no error, select ‘No error’.
o: The committee has careful
and has decided to take action.
considered the report which you sent us
questions.s:
Correct Answer:The committee has careful

Explanation:

  • The error lies in the phrase "has careful".

  • The verb "has" should be followed by a past participle or adverb, not an adjective like "careful".

  • The correct form is: "has carefully considered", where "carefully" is an adverb modifying the verb "considered".

✅ Correct sentence:
"The committee has carefully considered the report which you sent us and has decided to take action."

Therefore, the segment with the grammatical error is: The committee has careful.
